name: inspira-dither-shader

frames.best_why: Frame 1 shows the ordered-dot pattern across the whole landscape most evenly and cleanly.

tagline: A photo becomes crisp black-and-white dots and crosshatch patterns.
summary: A canvas that redraws an image in a choice of dither patterns: ordered dots, halftone blobs, noise or crosshatch, in grayscale, duotone or custom palettes.
appearance: A wide photo of hills and sky is reduced to hard black and white, built from tiny dots or blocky shapes. Under it sit two rows of small pill buttons for pattern and colour mode, one highlighted in each row.
behaviour: Choosing a pattern or colour button redraws the image immediately in that style. Brightness, contrast and threshold reshape how much turns black or white, and an optional loop animates the noise.
demo_content: Mountain landscape photo; buttons bayer, halftone, noise, crosshatch, grayscale, duotone, original, custom.
use_when: An image should take on a printed, one-bit or retro look and the pattern must be switchable live.
avoid_when: It redraws every pixel on the CPU, so large canvases or the animated noise mode can stutter.
customise: src, gridSize, ditherMode, colorMode, palette colours, brightness, contrast, threshold, objectFit and animated/speed are props; the patterns themselves are fixed.
weight_why: Redraws the whole image pixel by pixel on the CPU; only heavy when animated is on.

a11y.note: The canvas is labelled as an image but with a generic description, and the optional animation ignores reduced-motion.

issues: The mode buttons are small with low-contrast inactive labels.
polish_why: The dither itself is crisp, but the tiny button rows look like an unstyled demo control.
title: Dither Shader
